rationale: This is a cosmetic re-normalization of the archive's already-tested "CurrentDebt Accrual Burden" (dlc/at − dltt/at → dlc/lt), which produced weak evidence on both metrics, so no new economic content is being tested beyond accruals × short-maturity share.

The SUB(MUL(RANK(x),RANK(y)), MUL(RANK(NEG(x)),RANK(NEG(y)))) structure algebraically collapses to RANK(x)+RANK(y)−1, so the claimed "contrast interaction" is a purely additive blend of the accrual and debt-financing anomalies, and the oancf term appears in both legs (double-counting low operating cash flow) making it a near-duplicate of the archive's Accrual Financing Gap Strain.

Identical in structure to the archive's "DebtFunded Payout CashShortfall" with the only change being dropping prstkc from the payout term — a cosmetic variant rather than a substantively different mechanism.

Because RANK(NEG(x)) = 1 − RANK(x), the expression reduces exactly to RANK(accrual)+RANK(ACCEL(debt issuance))−1, so it eliminates rather than cleans the interaction in the already-tested "Accelerating DebtIssue Accrual Overhang" and contradicts its own stated conditional logic.

A genuine multiplicative interaction with correct sign handling of recch/invch that differs materially from the archive's equity-only and degenerate-contrast working-capital variants, though the financing-deficit leg reuses a heavily explored construct and coverage will remain thin.

Adding dp back to ib−oancf is an economically motivated sharpening toward working-capital accruals (closer to Sloan) and the level net-debt-issuance pairing has not been tested directly in the archive, but both legs are individually published anomalies so the novelty rests entirely on the interaction.
